NDT software in Tulsa: where the inspection work actually is

Tulsa still carries the Oil Capital nickname, but NDT work here covers a lot more than oil. A typical Tulsa inspection contractor splits its crews four ways. There is refinery work at the HF Sinclair Tulsa refinery on the west bank of the Arkansas River. There are midstream and pipeline jobs tied to operators headquartered in town, such as ONEOK and Williams. There is tank and terminal work around the Cushing storage hub, about an hour west. And there is shop inspection for the heat exchanger, air cooler, pressure vessel and skid fabricators spread through Tulsa, Broken Arrow, Sand Springs and the Port of Catoosa corridor. Add aviation component work near the large American Airlines maintenance base at Tulsa International, and one company can be shooting RT on a pipeline spread, running PAUT on exchanger nozzle welds and doing eddy current on aircraft parts in the same week.

That mix is why spreadsheets break down in Tulsa. Every client brings its own codes, its own report format and its own paperwork trail. Pipeline owners answer to PHMSA and, for intrastate lines, the Oklahoma Corporation Commission. Boilers and pressure vessels come under the Oklahoma Department of Labor. Radiography crews work under radioactive materials licences issued through Oklahoma's state programme. The Atlantis ERP solution keeps all of that in one system instead of six. This section covers how each ERP app applies to Tulsa inspection work.

ERP for NDT companies in Tulsa: the short answer

An ERP for NDT companies in Tulsa has to connect five things that usually live in separate places: technician certifications, instrument calibration, crew dispatch, field reports and billing. The Atlantis ERP puts them in one database, set up and supported by an ASNT NDT Level III who understands how inspection companies actually run.

Here is what that looks like on a real job. A dispatcher assigns a Level II UT technician and a flaw detector to a job at a Cushing tank farm. The system already knows whether that technician's certification is current, whether the instrument's calibration certificate has expired, and whether either one is already booked somewhere else. Once the report is approved, the timesheet hours, equipment and consumables flow to the invoice with the client PO attached. Nobody retypes the job number four times.

For small NDT companies in Tulsa with five to fifteen technicians, the main gain is time. The owner stops being the only person who knows whose certs expire next month. Larger contractors running several crews on turnaround work gain control: audit trails, locked procedure revisions and approval workflows that hold up when a client's QA auditor reviews your written practice.

Technician certification tracking software for Tulsa crews

Technician certification tracking deals with the most common audit finding in Tulsa shops: a technician on site whose certification or eye exam lapsed last month. The Certificates app records each technician's scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level, method and certifying body. It also holds issue, expiry and renewal dates, OJT hours, training hours and exam results, with the files attached.

Status is calculated automatically: active, expiring soon (within 90 days), expired or revoked. Vision tests are tracked separately. Each record holds near vision (Jaeger J1/J2), far vision, colour perception and contrast results, plus the examiner, clinic and expiry date. This matters in Tulsa because a lot of MT and PT work in the fabrication shops is fluorescent, and auditors do check colour perception records.

Daily checks create warning tasks 90 days before a cert or vision test expires. You can also set up daily email alerts to the QA manager and operations lead, with your own look-ahead days and resend interval. If someone logs timesheet hours for a technician whose certificate is not valid, the timesheet shows a warning. Each employee's NDT profile also holds radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry. Refinery contractor-safety teams ask for exactly that before an RT crew goes onto a unit.

Company certifications, such as ISO 9001 or client-specific accreditations, sit in the same place with their own alert days. When a refinery's contractor-qualification team asks for a document, you have it ready.

Calibration management software for Tulsa instrument fleets

Calibration management software should tell you which instruments are fit to go before a crew mobilises. In the Atlantis ERP, every flaw detector, PAUT unit, probe, yoke, eddy current instrument, densitometer and radiography accessory is tracked by serial number. Each record holds the equipment type, assigned person, condition, asset tag, firmware, accessories and lifecycle status: new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired or disposed.

Each calibration record captures the provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag, result (pass, fail or conditional) and next due date. The calibration certificate register stores the lab's accreditation number, the PDF and a valid, expiring or expired status, with expiry alerts sent to whoever you choose.

Equipment goes out and comes back through an issue and return workflow with supervisor and manager approval, and condition is recorded both ways. Say a Tulsa contractor is moving gear between a Broken Arrow shop job and a pipeline spread in eastern Oklahoma. Reservations with clash prevention stop the same UT set being promised to two crews. Consumables carry reorder levels and a low-stock flag, including couplant, MT particles, penetrant, developer, cleaner and PPE, so the crew heading to Cushing at 5 a.m. does not find an empty cabinet. The maintenance log records probe replacements, firmware updates and repairs, with condition before and after.

Crew dispatch software for turnarounds, pipeline spreads and Cushing tank work

Crew dispatch at a Tulsa NDT company means juggling spring and fall refinery turnarounds, pipeline construction spreads and steady shop work. The Team Assignments app treats every job as an assignment that moves through five stages: planned, dispatched, in field, submitted and closed. Each assignment holds site GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates.

The technician availability calendar shows who is assigned, on leave, in training, sick or unavailable, and overlaps are blocked. The system also blocks double-booking a technician or an instrument serial number. If the equipment assigned to a job is out of calibration, the dispatcher gets a warning. Calendar, kanban and list views show each technician's current assignment, utilisation percentage and next available date. So when a refinery calls on Thursday for a Monday start, one screen tells you who can actually go.

The Fleet app covers the vehicles. It records each vehicle's purpose, whether it is set up to carry radioactive sources, and its transport licence number and expiry. Vehicles are assigned to a project and driver with dates and mileage. When an RT crew is working night shift on a pipeline tie-in, knowing which truck is legal to carry the camera is not optional. Time Off requests feed the same availability calendar, so approved leave is never double-counted.

NDT reporting software for Tulsa exchanger shops, fabricators and refineries

NDT reporting software in Tulsa has to handle many report types at once. The Atlantis ERP includes 17: UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography. Each has its own numbering sequence.

Tulsa is known for heat exchanger and air-cooler fabrication. For those shops, one system holds IRIS and ECT reports for tubes, PAUT reports with focal laws for nozzle and header welds, PMI and hardness after welding, and PWHT records. RT reports capture source, technique, IQI type and placement. UT reports carry the probe calibration table. MT and PT reports capture technique, particle type, method and developer. Weld and job lines record defect type and orientation. Every report ends with an overall result: acceptable, not acceptable or acceptable with remarks.

Each report moves through draft, in progress, review, approved and sent. It carries inspector, reviewer and approver signatures, plus a third-party or authorised inspector's name and signature where the client requires one. Work order, WPS, contract, drawing, procedure and standard references are captured on the report. Company templates are versioned in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML with your logo. Excel templates fill automatically by mapping fields to cells, which helps when a refinery insists on its own spreadsheet format.

The offline field app works without signal, which is common on rural pipeline right-of-way. It stores drafts and photos locally, captures signatures on screen and syncs later. For more detail on the reporting product, see Digital Twin Reporting Software.

Procedures and written practice control

Any Tulsa NDT company working for refiners, pipeline operators or code shops depends on its procedures. The Procedures app keeps a register with each procedure's document number, revision, method, scope, material, applicable standard (such as ASME Section V), acceptance criteria and body text or uploaded file.

Procedures move from draft to submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejected and archived states as well. Prepared-by, reviewed-by and approved-by are recorded with dates. Approved revisions are locked, and every revision keeps a snapshot. So when an auditor asks which revision of your PAUT procedure was in force during last spring's turnaround, you can show it. An AI-assisted first draft can speed up writing a new procedure, but your Level III still reviews and approves it. Email reminders chase approvers who have pending approvals.

Reports reference the procedure, and project tasks carry procedure and WPS references. You can trace the chain from procedure to technician to report without digging through shared drives.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for Tulsa contractors

NDT quoting and invoicing software should let you price a job the way Tulsa clients buy it: by method, by day or shift, with equipment and consumables broken out. Quotations in the Atlantis ERP carry job type, site, project dates and applicable codes. NDT service products are flagged by method and category, you can apply a global discount if needed, and the quote goes out as a branded PDF. Clients can accept and sign online, and the quote converts to a sales order.

Invoices carry the NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with subtotals for labour, equipment and consumables. Each line holds cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours. Timesheet hours feed billing directly, with a billable flag and rate multiplier, and inspection, travel, standby and setup are logged as separate work types. That matters because unbilled turnaround standby is where many Tulsa contractors lose money today.

The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, outstanding invoices, bills and expenses over a 12-month view. Field expenses and per diems go through Expenses and can be re-billed to the job.

Inspection management software in Tulsa: dashboards, CRM and integrations

Inspection management software earns its keep when managers can see the whole operation in one view. KPI dashboards show calibration due and overdue, certs expiring and expired, and issued equipment overdue for return, next to the financial dashboard.

On the sales side, the CRM records service line, lead source, NDT service type, industry sector, site country and estimated technicians and days. Each lead gets an NDT lead score from 0 to 100, so your estimator knows which refinery or fabricator enquiry to chase first. Leads import from CSV, and a business card photographed at a Tulsa trade event becomes a CRM lead in one click.

You may already run other systems, such as QuickBooks for the books or a client's SAP or Maximo portal. The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and connects to SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections. The scope of each integration is agreed during implementation.

Affordable, customizable ERP for inspection companies in Tulsa: how implementation works

An affordable, customizable ERP for inspection companies in Tulsa is set up around your written practice, report formats and billing structure. It should not force you into someone else's process. The Atlantis ERP is quoted on request, sized to your company and set up by Atlantis NDT.

  1. Discovery. We review your written practice, current report templates, client list and how you bill: day rate, shift, unit or lump sum.
  2. Data load. We import technicians and certifications, vision tests, instruments and calibration certificates, procedures and clients.
  3. Templates. We rebuild your existing report and quote formats as versioned templates, including any client-mandated Excel layouts.
  4. Field rollout. Technicians install the offline app and run live jobs alongside the old process until the reports match.
  5. Integrations and training. We scope and build the API connections, then train office staff on dispatch, approvals and billing.

If you also need Level I, II or III training for new hires, Atlantis offers SNT-TC-1A-based training through an eLearning portal and the Practical NDT 3D simulator. Book a demo configured for a Tulsa NDT company.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT software for a small NDT company in Tulsa?

The best fit covers certifications, calibration, dispatch, reports and billing together, without needing a full-time administrator. The Atlantis ERP is configured to your written practice and report formats during implementation. A five-person Tulsa shop gets the same audit trail as a large contractor without building it from scratch.

Does the Atlantis ERP track SNT-TC-1A, CP-189 and client-specific qualifications?

Yes. Each certification records the scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level, method, certifying body, dates, OJT and training hours, exam results and attachments. Expiring-soon and expired status is set automatically. Client-specific qualifications can be recorded under the other scheme.

Can one system handle refinery, pipeline and aviation work?

Yes. Each project carries its own codes, scope, acceptance criteria and procedure references, and the 17 report types cover the methods used across those sectors. Each client can have its own report template.

How much does the Atlantis ERP cost for a Tulsa inspection company?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on your team size, the apps you need and any integrations, and it is positioned to be affordable for small and mid-sized NDT companies. Ask for a quote.

Does the field app work at rural pipeline and tank farm sites with no signal?

Yes. The field app is an installable web app. It stores drafts and photos on the device, captures on-screen signatures, previews the PDF and syncs when the technician is back in coverage.

Can it connect to QuickBooks or a client's SAP or Maximo system?

Yes. The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections. Each integration is scoped during implementation.
